(Edit: I didn't downvote you btw)
[jv] @BestTechAdvisor:
160Wh is the limt
It depends on the airline.
[BestTechAdvisor] @jv: These limits are set by the ICAO and are the same for every airline.
Airlines can approve or disapprove any item, including batteries, on a case-by-case basis, regardless of size. They can also set their own policies for anything and everything.
Many Airlines have updated their policies on batteries this year following updates from the ICAO, but afaik these policies have mostly been about not charging or discharging batteries during the flight, keeping batteries easily accessible (not in overhead lockers), etc.
The only airline I can find that appears to have introduced a blanket disapproval of >100Wh battery packs might be American Airlines… but it contradicts itself on the same page - it says 2 x 160Wh limit in one place, then 2 x 100Wh limit further down.
It's definitely not at all common, and 100% does not happen on domestic Australian Airlines such as Qantas, Virgin, and Jetstar.
[jv] @BestTechAdvisor:
These limits are set by the ICAO and are the same for every airline.
Airlines can and do refuse powerbanks >100Wh…
[BestTechAdvisor] @jv: Airlines can and do refuse power banks <100Wh too. I just said that:

[jv] @BestTechAdvisor:
